paper.title: More Adaptive Algorithms for Adversarial Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: combinatorial bandit problem with semi-bandit feedback
unmapped: action set X subset of {0,1}^K with at most K_0 arms per action
settings.definition_quote: In each round, the learner selects a subset of arms, denoted by a binary vector $b_t$ from a predefined action set $\mathcal{X}\subseteq \{0,1\}^K$, and suffers loss $b_t^\top \ell_t$, where $\ell_t \in [-1,1]^K$ is a loss vector decided by an adversary. ... we assume that the adversary is oblivious
In the special case of multi-armed bandit, the action set $\mathcal{X}$ is $\{\mathbf{e}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{e}_K\}$ ... receives the loss $\ell_{t,i_t}$.
in the adversarial setting, we have $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T] = \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{KL_{T,i^*}\ln T}+K\ln T)$ assuming non-negative losses.

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic setting with fixed gap (Adapting to Stochastic Bandits)
unmapped: exists arm a* with E[l_{t,i}-l_{t,a*} | l_1..l_{t-1}] >= Delta for all i != a* and all t (neither independence nor identical distribution required)
regret measured against empirically best arm i*, with expectation over losses
settings.definition_quote: there exists an arm $a^*$ and some fixed gap $\Delta > 0$ such that $\mathbb{E}_{\ell_t}\left[\ell_{t,i}-\ell_{t,a^*} | \ell_1, \ldots, \ell_{t-1}\right]\geq \Delta$ for all $i \neq a^*$ and $t\in[T]$.

settings.name_in_paper: two-player zero-sum game with bandit feedback
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Game-theoretic result: convergence of average strategies to Nash equilibrium value, not a regret bound for a single learner.
unmapped: players observe e_{i_t}^T G y_t (expected loss over opponent's randomness)
settings.definition_quote: we consider a setting where the feedbacks are the scalar values $\mathbf{e}_{i_t}^\top Gy_t$ and $x_t^\top G\mathbf{e}_{j_t}$ respectively

symbols.Err_star: E[sum_t sum_{i in b*} (l_{t,i} - m_{t,i})^2], squared prediction error on arms of best action
symbols.K_0: max number of arms an action can pick

source.label: cor:clear_corollary
source.quote: \textsc{Broad-OMD} with $a_{t,i}=6\eta_{t,i}w_{t,i}(\hat{\ell}_{t,i}-m_{t,i})^2$, any $m_{t,i} \in [-1, 1]$, ... and $\eta_{t,i}=\eta \leq \frac{1}{162K_0}$ enjoys the following regret bound: \mathbb{E}[\reg_T] \leq \frac{K\ln T}{\eta} + 6\eta\mathbb{E}[...] +\mathcal{O}(K_0).

results.notes: Leading terms exact, only K_0 term in O; recorded with O notation. Oblivious adversary so expected regret equals pseudo-regret vs fixed b*. Horizon: fixed eta algorithm does not use T.

symbols.Q_star: Q_{T,i*}: unnormalized variance of the best arm's losses

tuning: reservoir sampling with M = Theta(ln T)

source.label: cor:variance_bound
source.quote: \textsc{Broad-OMD} with reservoir sampling~\citep{hazan2011better}, ... and $\eta_{t,i}=\eta\leq \frac{1}{162}$ guarantees \mathbb{E}[\reg_T]= \mathcal{O}(\frac{K\ln T}{\eta}+\eta Q_{T,i^*} + K(\ln T)^2).

results.notes: Reservoir sampling M=Theta(ln T) requires T.

symbols.Q_star: Q_{T,i*}: unnormalized variance of the best arm's losses

tuning: eta optimally tuned in terms of Q_{T,i*} (unknown quantity)

source.label: cor:variance_bound
source.quote: With the optimal tuning of $\eta$, the regret is thus of order $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sqrt{KQ_{T,i^*}}+K\right)$.

results.notes: Requires oracle tuning of eta with Q_{T,i*}.

symbols.rho_star: E[rho_{T+1,i*}], expected final threshold of best arm
symbols.V_star: V_{T,i*}: first-order path-length of best arm

source.label: thm:path_length
source.quote: \textsc{Broad-OMD+} with $m_{t,i}=\ell_{\alpha_i(t), i}$ and $\eta_{1,i}=\eta\leq \frac{1}{810}$ guarantees \mathbb{E}[\reg_T ] \leq \frac{2K\ln T}{\eta} + \mathbb{E}[\rho_{T+1,i^*}]( \frac{-1}{40\eta\ln T} + 90\eta V_{T,i^*} ) + \mathcal{O}( 1 ) when $T\geq 3$.

results.notes: Exact except additive O(1); recorded with O notation.

symbols.V_star: V_{T,i*}: first-order path-length of best arm

source.label: thm:path_length
source.quote: Picking $\eta = \min\Big\{\frac{1}{810}, \frac{1}{60\sqrt{V_{T,i^*} \ln T}}\Big\}$ so that the second term is non-positive leads to $\mathbb{E}\left[\reg_T \right] = \tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( K\sqrt{V_{T,i^*}}+K \right)$.

symbols.K_0: max number of arms an action can pick

tuning: initial eta = 1/(162 K_0), halved on restart

source.label: thm:doubling_trick_theorem
source.quote: If conditions (ii) and (iii) in Theorem~\ref{lemma:second_order_regret_bound} hold, then Algorithm \ref{alg:doubling} guarantees \mathbb{E}[\reg_T]=\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{(K\ln T)\mathbb{E}[\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^Kw_{t,i}^2(\hat{\ell}_{t,i}-m_{t,i})^2]}+K_0K\ln T).

results.notes: Conditions are on estimator/prediction choices; algorithm-dependent quantity in bound.

symbols.V_sum: sum_i V_{T,i}: sum of first-order path-lengths of all arms

source.label: cor:path_length_bound_1
source.quote: \textsc{Broad-OMD} with $a_{t,i}=0$, $m_{t,i}=\ell_{\alpha_i(t),i}$, ... and $\eta_{t,i}=\eta\leq \frac{1}{162}$ guarantees \mathbb{E}[\reg_T]\leq\mathcal{O}(\frac{K\ln T}{\eta}) + 6\eta\sum_{i=1}^K V_{T,i} -\mathbb{E}[\sum_{t=2}^{T} \sum_{i=1}^K\frac{(w_{t,i}-w_{t-1,i})^2}{48\eta w_{t-1,i}^2} ]\leq \mathcal{O}( \frac{K\ln T}{\eta} + \eta\sum_{i=1}^K V_{T,i} ).

results.notes: Intermediate bound also contains a negative stability term (used for games).

symbols.V_sum: sum_i V_{T,i}: sum of first-order path-lengths of all arms

source.label: cor:path_length_bound_1
source.quote: Using the doubling trick (Algorithm~\ref{alg:doubling}), we achieve expected regret $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sqrt{K\sum_{i=1}^K V_{T,i}} + K\right)$.

symbols.X_T: E[sum_t sum_i (l_{t,i} 1{i_t=i} - w_{t,i} l_{t,i_t})^2], second-order excess loss quantity

source.label: thm:best of both
source.quote: \textsc{Broad-OMD} with $a_t = 0$, $m_{t,i}=\ell_{t,i_t}$, $\hat{\ell}_{t,i}=\frac{\ell_{t,i}\mathbbm{1}\{i_t=i\}}{w_{t,i}}$, and the doubling trick (Algorithm~\ref{alg:doubling}), guarantees \mathbb{E}[\reg_T]=\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{(K\ln T)\mathbb{E}[ \sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^K (\ell_{t,i}\mathbbm{1}\{i_t=i\}-w_{t,i}\ell_{t,i_t})^2 ]} + K\ln T ).

conditions: exists arm a* whose conditional expected loss is smaller than every other arm's by at least Delta at every round

source.label: thm:best of both
source.quote: This bound implies that in the stochastic setting, we have $\mathbb{E}\left[\reg_T\right] = \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{K\ln T}{\Delta}\right)$

results.notes: Regret vs empirically best arm i*, expectation over losses and learner randomness. Delta is a uniform gap lower bound. Environment mapped to adversarial_self_bounding (stochastically constrained adversary).

source.label: thm:best of both
source.quote: while in the adversarial setting, we have $\mathbb{E}\left[\reg_T\right] = \mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{KL_{T,i^*}\ln T}+K\ln T\right)$ assuming non-negative losses.

conditions: both players run Broad-OMD configured as in Corollary 9

source.label: thm:fast_convergence_theorem
source.quote: if both players run \textsc{Broad-OMD} configured as in Corollary~\ref{cor:path_length_bound_1} except that $\eta_{t,i}=\eta= (M+N)^{-\frac{1}{4}}T^{-\frac{1}{4}}$, then their expected average strategies converge to Nash equilibriums at the rate of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left((M+N)^{\frac{5}{4}}/T^{\frac{3}{4}}\right)$

results.notes: Quantity: duality gap of expected average strategies relative to game value.

cited_results.setting_description: adversarial multi-armed bandit, K arms, T rounds
